scope: Rename, do not restructure. Three edits in editorHtml() and one CSS class. No state key renamed, no storage column renamed, no field added or removed — only where a field sits and what its label says.

what_v36_changes.goals_is_mission: The field under Mission, Philosophy and Values was labelled Goals with the placeholder 'mission, not the full law' — the correction written into the hint instead of the label, while the value saves as ai_mission. It now reads Mission, with the hint 'what this conversation is for'. The state key goals and the column ai_mission are unchanged; nobody sees either.
what_v36_changes.scope_moves_to_mission: Scope was seventh in a seven-field Boundaries panel, behind Core values, Prohibitions, Interaction policy, Invariants and Defaults. It answers the question its new heading asks — what is this conversation for — and it reaches the model on every turn as Topic Scope, which it did not look like buried in that list.
what_v36_changes.identity_splits_into_three: The Identity panel held filing details (id, label, version, install-private), a nameplate (name, role) and probe answers (identity lock, the two probe lines) in one column, which read as one list of equals. Same fields, same keys, three labelled groups: Filing, Nameplate, Under probe.
what_v36_changes.name_hint: The Name hint read 'chat header; this personality introduces itself as this name'. It now reads 'what it is called — BubblyBetty, Tech Agent', because the altitude was the confusion: a name is a label, not the identity.

gate_added: check_attachment_save.php now pins that every stored field a floscAdmin is expected to fill has an editor — name, role, goals, prohibitions, scope — and that Scope sits with Mission and is labelled Mission rather than Goals. ai_topic_scope reaches the model on every turn and spent this whole cycle with no path from the designer to the database; a field read at runtime with no input anywhere is that bug's shape.
